Chapter Three: Building Credibility and Positioning as an Expert
So, you’ve got your message nailed down. Now comes the real challenge—getting people to trust you.
In the world of advice and expertise, credibility is like currency. It’s what opens doors and gets people to actually listen, learn, and invest in what you have to offer.
But here’s the thing: you don’t need a fancy title or a wall full of degrees to be credible. What really matters is a mix of your personal results, the stories and testimonials you can share, and how well you communicate the value of what you do.
Think of positioning yourself as an expert as a process—one that happens both inside and out.
Let’s start from the inside. Internally, it’s all about seeing yourself as a guide or mentor, not just waiting for someone to call you a “guru.”
Maybe you’ve thought, “Who am I to teach anyone?” But the truth is, your unique perspective and the progress you’ve made—no matter how small—can inspire others.
Confidence in your own journey is the first step to inspiring confidence in those who are listening.
Externally, you build credibility by showing proof and delivering real value, over and over again.
How do you do that?
Well, start by sharing your personal stories—not just the highs, but the setbacks too. Collect testimonials from people who’ve benefited from your advice, even if it’s just a handful at first. Show off your results, whether it’s before-and-after photos, measurable improvements, or simply positive changes you’ve helped create. And put yourself out there: write articles, make videos, or share insights that show what you know.
Here’s a helpful way to picture it. Imagine credibility as a three-legged stool. One leg is your personal experience and results. Another is social proof—testimonials and endorsements from others. And the third leg? That’s your demonstrated knowledge, the content you create and the way you teach. Each leg props up the others, giving you a solid platform to stand on.
Think about someone who’s lost weight and kept it off. They can share their own story, include feedback from friends who tried their method, and maybe even publish a guide or a video series explaining what worked. See how those three legs work together?
There’s something else just as important: transparency.
Don’t be afraid to talk about the tough parts—those moments when things didn’t go as planned, and what you learned from it. People connect with honesty, not perfection. When you share the real journey, bumps and all, you become relatable—and that builds genuine trust.
Positioning yourself as an expert also means promoting yourself, but in a way that feels real—not boastful. Make it easy for people to see your value. That might mean building a simple, professional website, posting regular updates on social media, or joining communities where your voice can be heard.
Over time, as more people benefit from your message and share their own stories, your credibility will grow on its own.
The key is to stay consistent, stay authentic, and always focus on helping others.
That’s how you move from being just another voice out there, to becoming the trusted guide people turn to for inspiration and advice.
